newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian protest for opposition member's freedom.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian protest for opposition member's freedom.

text.p: Dozens of Cambodians gathered outside parliament and the justice ministry on Wednesday to demand the release of an opposition member held on murder charges.

Sam Rainsy, head of the officially unrecognised Khmer Nation Party (KNP), and other top opposition leaders handed a list of demands to five members of parliament and Secretary of State for Justice Ouk Vithun.
The demands included the immediate release of Srun Vong Vannak, KNP security chief and steering committee member, who was arrested on February 14.
He and two other men were charged last week with involvement in the November 19 murder of co-Premier Hun Sen's brother-in-law outside a Phnom Penh restaurant.
The protesters pledged to forward their demands to co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and said they would try to ensure legal representation for Srun Vong Vannak.
The list of demands, distributed to reporters, said Srun Vong Vannak should be given access to his family and a lawyer and demanded that his health and safety be guaranteed in detention.
It also said any extorted confession could not be used against him in court and insisted that the Phnom Penh municipal police chief be prosecuted for illegal confinement.

Srun Vong Vannak's parents met him on Wednesday for the first time since his arrest, his father said. He added that his son denied involvement in the murder and told them he had not been ill treated in the detention centre.
Son Chhay, one of two MPs who visited the detainee on Tuesday, said he looked scared and was being held in a small, dark room.

London-based Amnesty International on Tuesday said it feared for the safety of Srun Vong Vannak and urged people to send messages to the government calling for him to be given access to his family and a lawyer of his choice. People should also seek information on his health and urge authorities to uphold his rights in detention, Amnesty said.

Sam Rainsy wrote to King Norodom Sihanouk on Monday appealing for a royal order to grant Srun Vong Vannak access to legal counsel. The king, in a letter made public on Tuesday, sought Justice Minister Chem Snguon's advice on what he could do.
The KNP leader says his security chief's arrest was engineered by Hun Sen in a bid to destabilise his party.
The KNP recently formed an alliance with the royalist FUNCINPEC party, main partner and rival of Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party in the uneasy coalition government formed in 1993.
